abstract.text:
In this paper, we will apply the tools from number theory and modular forms
to the study of the Seiberg-Witten theory. We will express the holomorphic functions a, aD,
which generate the lattice Z = nea + nm aD, (ne, nm) ∈ Z2 of central charges, in terms of
the periods of the Legendre family of elliptic curves. Thus we will be able to compute the
transformations of the quotient aD /a under the action of the modular group PSL(2, Z). We
will show the Schwarzian derivative of the quotient aD /a with respect to the complexified
coupling constant is given by the theta functions. We will also compute the scalar curvature
of the moduli space of the N = 2 supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory, which is shown to be
asymptotically flat near the perturbative limit.

by using the holomorphic properties of the theory together with their monodromy behaviors
near certain singularities.

sections.summary: Sets up the N=2 SU(2) Seiberg-Witten theory, the moduli space, the periods a and aD, and the paper's motivation from number theory and modular forms.

source_span.start_text: 2. The Legendre family of elliptic curves

sections.summary: Reviews the Legendre family of elliptic curves, its periods, hypergeometric expansions, and the Picard-Fuchs equation.
sections.title: Legendre family and Picard-Fuchs periods

source_span.start_text: 3. The modular lambda function and theta functions

sections.summary: Develops the modular lambda function, its relation to the period quotient τ, theta-function identities, and the normalized Yukawa coupling.
sections.title: Modular lambda, theta functions, and Yukawa coupling

source_span.start_text: 4. The meromorphic Seiberg-Witten oneform and its periods

sections.summary: Transforms the meromorphic Seiberg-Witten oneform to the Legendre family, defines BPS periods π0 and π1, and relates them to a, aD, and τsw.
sections.title: Meromorphic Seiberg-Witten oneform and BPS periods

source_span.start_text: 5. The Schwarzian derivative of the Seiberg-Witten period

sections.summary: Studies modular transformations of ϕ and πi, the fixed point λ=1/2, and computes the Schwarzian derivative of aD/a as a theta function.
sections.title: Schwarzian derivative and modular transformations

source_span.end_text:
The behavior of the Seiberg-Witten period ϕ at
λ = 1 can be analyzed similarly, which is related to the λ = 0 case by an S-transformation.
source_span.start_text: 6. Great Picard’s Theorem and the non-perturbative limit

sections.summary: Applies Great Picard's Theorem to show the quotient aD/a takes real values near the non-perturbative limits u = ±1.

source_span.end_text:

the property that λ = ∞ (u = ∞) is a perturbative limit of the N = 2 supersymmetric
Yang-Mills theory.

sections.title: Scalar curvature of the moduli space
